title: The Italian Renaissance
description: Harmony, perspective, and humanism from the rebirth of classical ideals.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Virgin and Child with an Angel
items.description_narrative: Mary holds the Christ child close, his hand reaching up to touch her face as she looks down at him with a gentle smile. An angel with folded hands gazes up at the pair from the left, beside a small vase of flowers, while an arched window behind them frames a distant landscape and a round rose window. Botticelli painted this devotional panel between 1475 and 1485; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: madonna, christ child, angel, tempera panel, devotional painting

items.title: Virgin and Child with Two Angels
items.description_narrative: Two winged angels in flowing rose robes present the standing Christ Child to his mother beneath a dark canopy of trees, its branches parting in places to reveal a pale, distant landscape. Painted within a round tondo panel, the composition draws the eye toward her downcast gaze and the child's outstretched arms.
items.tags: virgin and child, angels, tempera panel, tondo, florentine renaissance, devotional, religious art
items.physical_dimensions: Diam.: 34.4 cm (13 1/2 in.); Framed: Diam.: 44.5 cm (17 1/2 in.)

items.title: Allegory of Venus and Cupid
items.description_narrative: A nude woman and a clothed woman face each other closely, their hands joined around a pair of arrows, while a winged child looks up between them. Behind them, dim figures raise a basket of doves and a cluster of grapes against a dark blue sky. This allegory of Venus and Cupid was painted around 1600 by a follower of Titian; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: allegory, venus and cupid, mythology, figures, oil painting, venetian

items.title: Portrait of a Lady
items.description_narrative: A woman gazes calmly outward, one hand raised to her chest with fingers lightly touching a bit of lace at her collar. Loose curls frame her face, and a white lace cuff is the only bright note against her deep brown dress and the near-black background. This portrait, from Titian's circle, dates to the 16th century; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: portrait, woman, lace, dark background, oil painting, venetian

items.title: Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: A long panel unfolds three scenes across a checkerboard-tiled courtyard: at left, small groups gather in a rocky landscape; at center, women attend a new mother in bed indoors, one holding an infant and another approaching with a vessel; at right, elderly figures with walking sticks greet a woman at a grand doorway. Bartolomeo di Giovanni painted this narrative panel in 1490/95; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: narrative panel, saint john the baptist, architecture, tempera panel, early renaissance

items.title: The Nativity
items.description_narrative: A man kneels in a deep red robe, hands raised, opposite a woman in blue who bends in prayer over a swaddled infant lying in the grass between them. Above them, three angels hover with wide pink-lined wings, and two more angels stand quietly at her shoulder. A wide valley opens behind the group, dotted with buildings, hills, and tiny distant figures on horseback. Fra Bartolomeo painted this Nativity between 1504 and 1507; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: nativity, mary and joseph, angels, christ child, religious scene, oil painting

items.title: Alessandro de' Medici
items.description_narrative: A young man gazes slightly off to the side, his dark hair framing a pale, intently lit face against a nearly black background. He wears a dark cloak over chainmail, with a sliver of white collar and red trim visible at the neck. Pontormo painted this portrait of Alessandro de' Medici in the mid-1530s; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: portrait, medici, mannerism, chainmail, young man, oil painting

items.title: Christ Carrying the Cross
items.description_narrative: Christ, crowned with thorns and dressed in white, bears the weight of a large wooden cross that cuts diagonally across the composition. Two men crowd close behind him — one bareheaded, the other in a dark metal helmet — while a small landscape with a distant crowd is visible through a gap at the right edge. Sebastiano del Piombo painted this close, half-length scene in the 1510s; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: christ, crucifixion narrative, religious scene, oil panel, high renaissance, close composition

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.description_narrative: Christ hangs on the cross beneath a small sign reading INRI, his head haloed and tilted toward a grieving woman at left. A young man in green and rose robes stands at right, gesturing toward the scene, while a bare skull rests at the foot of the cross among scattered rocks. Carlo Crivelli painted this crucifixion around 1487; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: crucifixion, christ, religious scene, tempera panel, early renaissance, skull

items.title: Saint John the Baptist Entering the Wilderness
items.description_narrative: A haloed figure in a pink robe seems to float down a steep, craggy mountain path, hands clasped in a gesture of resolve. Below, another haloed figure in matching pink steps through the archway of a small white building, with a walled city and neat checkerboard fields spreading across the valley beyond. Giovanni di Paolo painted this panel between 1455 and 1460; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: saint john the baptist, wilderness, mountain landscape, tempera panel, religious scene
items.credit_line: fAF3o1FJojE54g at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Ecce Agnus Dei
items.description_narrative: A haloed man in a rose mantle gestures toward another haloed figure standing at right in a pink robe with hands raised in blessing. A cluster of onlookers in orange and blue robes crowds close at left, while jagged grey rock formations and a walled town rise beneath a reddish sky. Giovanni di Paolo painted this panel between 1455 and 1460; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: john the baptist, christ, religious scene, tempera panel, sienese, landscape
items.credit_line: PQFQBhH5OZFS2A at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Assassination and Funeral of Julius Caesar
items.medium: Tempera on panel, transferred to canvas mounted on pressed hardboard and cradled
items.description_narrative: A long, narrow panel unfolds two scenes side by side: at left, richly dressed men in gold and red gather indoors around a fallen figure, while at right a much larger crowd fills a colonnaded courtyard, some in swirling, athletic poses. At the far right, mourners in dark robes cluster around a draped bier beneath a canopy. This narrative panel dates from the mid-15th century; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: cassone panel, roman history, crowd scene, procession, narrative painting, tempera

items.title: The Last Communion of Saint Jerome
items.description_narrative: A gaunt, kneeling old man receives the host from a bishop in a rose-colored cope, his hands raised in supplication and his beard long and unkempt. Behind them, an altar holds a small crucifix flanked by tall palm fronds, and two young acolytes in white hold lit candles at the far left. Monks in dark robes look on from the right, all gathered inside a plain, timbered chapel.
items.tags: saint jerome, last communion, religious scene, tempera panel, monks, altar
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: The Annunciation
items.description_narrative: A winged angel kneels before a haloed woman in a colonnaded interior, gold leaf catching light along his feathers and her halo. The panel is painted in tempera and gold on wood, dated to around 1490, and belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: annunciation, angel, religious art, tempera, gold leaf, renaissance, interior
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Mona Lisa
items.description_narrative: A woman in dark robes sits with her hands folded, a faint smile playing across her face as she gazes steadily outward. Behind her, a hazy, winding landscape of rocky cliffs, a bridge, and distant water recedes into blue-green atmosphere. Leonardo da Vinci painted this portrait in the early 1500s; it belongs to the Louvre.
items.tags: portrait, mona lisa, sfumato, landscape background, oil painting
items.credit_line: C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition: image page

items.title: The Birth of Venus
items.description_narrative: Venus stands nude on a giant scallop shell, her long hair swept by the wind as she drifts to shore. At left, two windswept figures embrace mid-air, scattering pink blossoms as they blow her toward land, while at right a robed woman waits to wrap a floral cloak around her. Botticelli painted this in the 1480s; it belongs to the Uffizi Gallery.
items.tags: birth of venus, mythology, venus, shell, wind figures, tempera, renaissance

items.title: The Creation of Adam
items.description_narrative: God, borne aloft in a swirl of drapery and attendant figures, reaches out to touch the outstretched hand of Adam, who lies reclining on a green hillside below. The scene sits within the painted architecture of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, framed by nude figures and bronze-toned medallions on either side. Michelangelo painted this fresco around 1511.
items.tags: creation of adam, fresco, sistine chapel, religious scene, ceiling painting
items.credit_line: Own work Burkhard Mücke Taken on 18 October 2017

items.title: The School of Athens
items.description_narrative: Raphael painted this fresco in 1512, part of the High Renaissance. It depicts a grand hall filled with classical philosophers gathered beneath vaulted archways, some conversing in groups, others reading or writing on the marble steps.
items.tags: fresco, high renaissance, philosophy, architecture, classical antiquity, raphael, group portrait
items.credit_line: "School of Athens" by Raphael, Raphael Rooms, Vatican Museum Complete indexed photo collection at WorldHistoryPics.com.

items.title: The Last Supper
items.description_narrative: Christ sits at the center of a long table, palms open, as the twelve apostles react around him in small clustered groups, some recoiling, others leaning in to speak. Three arched windows behind him open onto a distant hazy landscape, and the table is scattered with bread, dishes, and cups. This mural was painted between 1495 and 1498.
items.tags: last supper, christ, apostles, religious scene, mural, renaissance

items.title: Primavera
items.description_narrative: Nine figures move through a dark grove of orange trees: a man in red reaches up with a sword at left, three women in sheer white robes join hands in a dance beside him, and a woman with flowers scattered across her patterned gown strides in from the right, pursued by a pale blue-toned figure. At center, a woman in red and white gestures gently, a blindfolded winged child aiming an arrow just above her head. This allegorical scene is by Sandro Botticelli, painted between 1480 and 1485.
items.tags: primavera, mythology, allegory, dancing figures, tempera panel

items.title: Venus of Urbino
items.description_narrative: A nude woman reclines on a white sheet, one hand holding a small bouquet of roses and the other resting lightly at her hip, meeting the viewer's gaze directly. A small dog sleeps curled at the foot of the bed, while in the background two women search through a chest beneath a window opening onto a column and potted plant. Titian painted this in 1538; it belongs to the Uffizi Gallery.
items.tags: venus of urbino, reclining nude, interior, small dog, oil painting

items.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
items.description_narrative: Bacchus leaps from his chariot in mid-air, his pink cloak billowing behind him as he catches sight of a woman on the shore who turns back in alarm, one hand raised. Two spotted wildcats pull the chariot, and behind them revelers carrying cymbals fill the procession under a brilliant blue sky. Titian painted this mythological scene between 1520 and 1523; it belongs to the National Gallery.
items.tags: mythology, bacchus, ariadne, procession, wildcats, oil painting, renaissance
items.credit_line: Own work Joyofmuseums Taken on 16 July 2018

items.title: The Wedding at Cana
items.description_narrative: Veronese fills this immense canvas with a crowded Venetian banquet: musicians tune instruments in the foreground while servants pour wine from tall jugs and dogs wander beneath the tables. Grand classical columns and a balustrade lined with onlookers rise against a cloud-streaked sky. The scene reimagines the biblical wedding at Cana as a lavish feast on a canvas spanning nearly ten meters across.
items.tags: banquet, venetian, oil on canvas, religious art, mannerism, crowd scene, architecture

items.title: The Last Judgment
items.description_narrative: Christ stands at the center raising one arm in judgment, encircled by a dense mass of nude figures ascending toward heaven on the left and tumbling downward on the right. Near the top, angels strain to carry a large wooden cross and a column, while at the bottom a crucified figure and a boat of huddled souls appear above a row of candles. Michelangelo painted this fresco in the 16th century; it belongs to the Vatican Museums.
items.tags: last judgment, fresco, sistine chapel, religious scene, crowd of figures

items.title: Virgin of the Rocks
items.medium: Oil on panel, transferred to canvas
items.description_narrative: Mary kneels in a rocky grotto, one hand raised over an infant at left who bears a reed cross, while the Christ Child sits at right beside a watchful, folded-wing angel. Jagged stone pinnacles frame a hazy view of water and distant blue peaks, their edges dissolving into soft shadow. The painting depicts the Virgin Mary with the Christ Child.
items.tags: virgin mary, christ child, john the baptist, angel, rocky grotto, renaissance, devotional

items.title: The Sistine Madonna
items.description_narrative: Mary stands on a bed of clouds holding the Christ child, flanked by a kneeling man in a gold and white robe at left and a woman in green and gold at right. Below them, two winged children rest their chins on their folded arms, gazing upward, while heavy green curtains part on either side to frame the scene. Raphael painted this altarpiece around 1512 to 1513; it belongs to the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden.
items.tags: sistine madonna, mary and christ child, putti, altarpiece, oil painting
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — CgEiMJRg7ZS6DA (Original text: Google Arts & Culture)

items.title: Pallas and the Centaur
items.description_narrative: A woman in an olive-branch-patterned gown grips a centaur by his hair, holding him still as he looks up with a wary, pleading expression. She carries a tall halberd in her other hand, while the centaur holds a bow and arrows against ancient ruined columns behind them. This mythological scene is by Sandro Botticelli, painted around 1482; it belongs to the Uffizi Gallery.
items.tags: mythology, pallas, centaur, allegory, tempera, renaissance

items.title: The Battle of San Romano
items.medium: Egg tempera with oil on poplar panel
items.description_narrative: Lances crisscross at sharp angles above a dense crush of knights on armored horses, their trappings in bold red, white, and gold patterns. In the middle distance, tiny figures duel and hunt across a patterned brown countryside, while broken lances and a fallen rider lie scattered in the foreground. This battle scene, showing the Battle of San Romano, was painted by Paolo Uccello around 1456.
items.tags: battle scene, cavalry, lances, early renaissance, tempera panel

items.title: The Lamentation over the Dead Christ
items.description_narrative: The dead Christ lies foreshortened on a marble slab, his pierced feet closest to the viewer, as two mourners weep quietly at his side. Andrea Mantegna painted this Lamentation in tempera around 1483. It is held in the Pinacoteca di Brera.
items.tags: mantegna, lamentation, christ, foreshortening, tempera, religious, renaissance, brera
items.credit_line: Pinacoteca di Brera, inv. 352; Wikidata Q546297

items.title: Virgin and Child with the Young Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: Mary smiles gently down at the Christ child seated on her lap, who reaches out toward a young boy kneeling before them with a small reed cross. A leafy trellis heavy with fruit rises behind her on one side, while a soft landscape with distant hills and water opens on the other. Correggio painted this around 1515; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: madonna, christ child, saint john the baptist, landscape, oil panel

items.title: Tarquin and Lucretia
items.description_narrative: A muscular man grips a woman by the wrist and hair, pulling her back as she twists away, one hand raised in protest, pearls scattered loose at her throat. Rich red and dark velvet drapery tumbles across the bed around them, with a sword lying discarded on the floor below. Tintoretto painted this dramatic scene between 1578 and 1580; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: tarquin and lucretia, mannerism, dramatic scene, oil painting, roman history

items.title: Annunciation
items.description_narrative: A haloed angel with rainbow-colored wings kneels before a blue-robed woman inside an arched cloister that opens onto a garden. Wikimedia Commons identifies the scene as an Annunciation by Fra Angelico.
items.tags: annunciation, angel, religious art, cloister, fra angelico, renaissance

items.title: Ghent Altarpiece: Adoration of the Mystic Lamb
items.description_narrative: A white lamb stands on an altar at the center of a wide green meadow, blood flowing from its breast into a chalice, as a dove radiates light directly above. Crowds converge from both sides — prophets and patriarchs with books at left, robed figures with palm branches at right — while bishops in red and gold and a line of other clergy gather in the distance. An octagonal fountain flows in the immediate foreground.
items.tags: adoration, lamb, altarpiece, crowd scene, meadow, religious scene

items.title: The Annunciation
items.description_narrative: A blue-robed woman stands in a vaulted stone doorway, an open book in her hands, as a red-robed angel kneels just outside on the threshold. Behind the angel, a tall arched window opens onto a distant riverside town, and a ray of light touches down near the woman's feet carrying a small dove. Ornate tile work runs along the floor between them.
items.tags: annunciation, doorway, angel, riverside view, tile floor, religious scene
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Portrait of a Young Man
items.description_narrative: A young man in an elaborately slashed black doublet stands with one hand on his hip, the other resting on a red marble plinth beside a small book. A black beret sits at an angle on his head, and a doorway and carved stone corbel frame the cool grey interior behind him. This portrait was painted in the 1530s; it belongs to The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: portrait, young man, mannerism, doublet, oil painting, interior
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Jacob Willemsz van Veen (1456–1535), the Artist's Father
items.description_narrative: An elderly man with grey hair and a weathered, deeply lined face turns slightly toward the viewer, wearing a large dark fur cap and a black cloak fastened with three buttons. Below the portrait, a painted banner carries a lengthy inscription in ornate lettering, ending in a date. This portrait was painted in 1532; it belongs to The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: portrait, elderly man, fur cap, inscription, oil painting, dutch renaissance
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Hermann von Wedigh III (died 1560)
items.description_narrative: A young man in a black coat trimmed with fur and a matching cap rests his folded hands on a green-covered table, a small leather-bound book beside him and another tucked in his sleeve. Gold lettering on the deep blue background records his age and the year of the painting. Hans Holbein the Younger painted this portrait in 1532; it belongs to The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: portrait, young man, northern renaissance, oil painting, inscription
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Portrait of Giuliano de' Medici
items.description_narrative: A man in profile wears a deep red robe against an open doorway, half-closed eyes cast downward and dark curling hair framing his face. A small brown bird perches quietly at the base of the portrait, tucked into the corner beside his shoulder. This is a portrait of Giuliano de' Medici, painted by Botticelli between about 1478 and 1480; it belongs to the National Gallery of Art.
items.tags: portrait, giuliano de medici, profile, tempera panel, renaissance

items.title: Portrait of a Youth
items.description_narrative: A young man with long wavy hair and a red cap gazes steadily at the viewer, one hand raised to his chest against a dark background. Sandro Botticelli painted this portrait in tempera around 1483. It is part of the Andrew W. Mellon collection.
items.tags: portrait, botticelli, youth, renaissance, tempera, red cap, male figure, italian
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: Venus and the Three Graces Presenting Gifts to a Young Woman
items.description_narrative: A cluster of women in flowing pastel robes gather at left, one holding a blank tablet, as they approach a woman in a rich red gown who reaches out to accept a folded cloth. A small child in orange walks toward them at the lower right, and the painted plaster surface itself is cracked and worn with age. Botticelli painted this fresco in the 1480s; it belongs to the Louvre.
items.tags: fresco, women, allegory, wedding scene, early renaissance

items.title: Adoration of the Magi (Uffizi)
items.description_narrative: A woman sits enthroned beneath a ruined timber shelter, holding an infant as an elderly kneeling king reaches to kiss his foot. A crowd of richly dressed onlookers in red, blue, and gold fills the foreground and both sides, some turning to converse while others gaze toward the holy family. Crumbling stone walls and classical columns frame the scene under a pale sky. This Adoration of the Magi is by Sandro Botticelli, painted between about 1474 and 1476.
items.tags: adoration of the magi, crowd scene, medici, ruins, religious scene, tempera panel

items.title: Mystic Nativity
items.description_narrative: Rows of angels dance hand in hand beneath a golden arch above a thatched stable, where shepherds and animals gather around a swaddled infant while small winged devils flee into rocky crevices below. Botticelli painted this Mystic Nativity in 1500; it now hangs in the National Gallery.
items.tags: nativity, angels, religious art, botticelli, renaissance, apocalypse imagery
items.credit_line: National Gallery, London, NG1034; Wikidata Q974674

items.title: The Virgin and Child with Saint John and Two Angels (Studio of Botticelli)
items.description_narrative: In a circular composition, two winged angels reach up to lower a golden crown onto a woman's head as she holds a child, who reaches toward a young haloed boy kneeling at right. Roses climb a trellis behind them, and the angels' red and gold robes echo the flowers' color. This panel is from the workshop of Sandro Botticelli, made around 1495; it belongs to the National Gallery.
items.tags: madonna, coronation, angels, saint john, tempera panel, tondo
items.credit_line: 1. Art UK: entry 1160012. National Gallery, London - online catalogue.

items.title: Fortitude
items.description_narrative: A woman in ornate armor and a flowing red robe sits enthroned, holding a ceremonial rod and gazing outward with a solemn expression. Sandro Botticelli painted this personification of Fortitude in tempera on panel around 1475. It is held in the Uffizi Gallery.
items.tags: fortitude, botticelli, allegory, virtue, renaissance, tempera, uffizi, armor

items.title: Madonna and Child with Five Angels
items.description_narrative: Mary, wrapped in deep blue, holds the Christ child on her lap as he reaches toward fruit offered by a winged angel at left. Three more angels crowd close at right, one holding a leafy sprig, their pale faces turned toward the holy pair. Botticelli painted this devotional panel in the 1470s; it is part of the Louvre's collection.
items.tags: madonna, christ child, angels, tempera panel, devotional painting, louvre

items.title: Bardi Altarpiece (Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist and John the Evangelist)
items.description_narrative: The enthroned Madonna holds an infant who reaches toward her, flanked by two haloed saints — one lean and weathered in a rough fur mantle with a reed cross, the other elderly with a flowing beard, holding a book. Dense foliage, lilies, and small vases of flowers rise behind the throne, and a tiny painted crucifix rests on a ledge below. This altarpiece, attributed to Sandro Botticelli, was painted between 1484 and 1485.
items.tags: altarpiece, madonna, saints, tempera panel, religious scene, florentine renaissance
items.credit_line: This file was derived from: Sandro Botticelli - Madonna with Saints - Google Art Project.jpg:

items.title: Adoration of the Christ Child with Saint John (Botticelli or Workshop)
items.description_narrative: Mary kneels in the foreground, hands joined in prayer as she gazes down at the infant Christ lying on a bed of straw and cloth. Behind them, a young figure in a red robe stands holding a small reed cross, framed by rocky outcrops that open onto a distant, hazy river landscape. This adoration scene is attributed to Sandro Botticelli or his workshop, made around 1490; it belongs to the Landesmuseum Hannover.
items.tags: adoration, madonna, christ child, saint john, tempera panel, religious scene, workshop attribution

items.title: The Calumny of Apelles (detail: Truth)
items.description_narrative: A nude woman points upward with one hand while gesturing toward herself with the other, her long hair unbound, standing before classical statues set in shell-topped niches. Beside her, a hooded old woman in black stands hunched, arms crossed, gazing sideways. This is a detail from The Calumny of Apelles, painted by Botticelli around 1495.
items.tags: allegory, truth, calumny of apelles, classical sculpture, tempera panel, detail
items.credit_line: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202.

items.title: Virgin and Child with the Young Saint John (School of Botticelli)
items.description_narrative: In this black-and-white reproduction, Mary sits with the Christ child in her lap, his hand raised to touch his own chin as he looks toward a young boy nestled close beside them. A rolling landscape with a tree and birds in flight opens at the left, while both Mary and the child carry faint haloes. This devotional panel is from the school of Botticelli; it belongs to the Gemäldegalerie Berlin.
items.tags: madonna, christ child, saint john, monochrome, tempera panel

items.title: The Annunciation (Workshop of Botticelli)
items.description_narrative: A winged angel kneels at left, one hand raised in greeting and the other holding a flowering branch, while a woman kneels opposite with her hand pressed to her chest, eyes lowered. Between them, an arched opening frames a distant bridge and hills, and a curtained bed is visible in a side chamber at right. This Annunciation is from the workshop of Sandro Botticelli; it belongs to the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin.
items.tags: annunciation, angel, mary, architecture, workshop attribution, religious scene

items.title: Young Man Before the Seven Liberal Arts
items.description_narrative: A young man steps forward to greet a semicircle of women personifying the Liberal Arts, one enthroned above the rest in flowing red drapery. The plaster surface is worn and patched with loss along the lower edge, visible evidence of its life as a wall fresco. Painted at Villa Lemmi near Florence, it was later transferred to the Louvre.
items.tags: fresco, liberal arts, allegory, florentine, renaissance, villa lemmi, procession
items.credit_line: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202. Web Gallery of Art: Image Info about artworkwga QS:P11807,"b/botticel/5allegor/52lemmi"

items.title: Pastoral Concert
items.description_narrative: Two clothed young men sit close together in conversation, one cradling a lute, while a nude woman pours water from a glass vessel into a stone well at left and another nude woman with a flute sits at right, gazing away. Trees frame the scene, and a distant shepherd tends sheep on a hillside path. This pastoral scene is attributed to Titian and Giorgione, painted around 1510; it belongs to the Louvre.
items.tags: pastoral concert, nude figures, lute, landscape, venetian, oil painting
items.credit_line: Retouched from File:Le Concert champêtre, by Titian, from C2RMF.jpg, originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition: image page

items.title: Venus with an Organ Player
items.description_narrative: A nude woman reclines against red pillows, a winged child nestled against her shoulder with one arm around her, while at left an organist at his pipes turns to look back at her. Beyond them, a wide landscape with hills and small buildings unfolds under a cloud-streaked sky. Titian painted this around 1555; it belongs to the Museo del Prado.
items.tags: venus, organ player, cupid, landscape, oil painting

items.title: Girl in a Fur
items.description_narrative: A young woman turns to meet the viewer's gaze, one bare shoulder emerging from a dark fur wrap she clutches at her chest. A string of pearls circles her neck, and a jeweled band holds back her hair, catching the only real light in an otherwise deeply shadowed portrait. Titian painted this around 1535; it belongs to the Kunsthistorisches Museum.
items.tags: portrait, fur, pearls, young woman, oil painting, venetian
items.credit_line: uAFWZO04aJE2SA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Portrait of Alfonso I d'Este
items.description_narrative: A heavyset, bearded man in a red velvet robe trimmed with dark fur rests one hand on a wide-brimmed hat and the other on the hilt of a sword at his waist. A gold embroidered sleeve peeks from beneath his outer robe, and his gaze is direct and steady. This is a portrait of Alfonso I d'Este by Titian.
items.tags: portrait, alfonso deste, nobility, oil painting, este family

items.title: Diana and Actaeon
items.description_narrative: A hunter pulls back a red curtain to reveal Diana and her nymphs bathing beside a stone fountain in a wooded glade, as a startled attendant ducks behind a pillar. Titian painted this mythological scene in oil on canvas in the 1550s. It is held in the National Gallery of Scotland.
items.tags: mythology, diana, actaeon, titian, renaissance, oil painting, nymphs, nudes

items.title: Diana and Callisto
items.description_narrative: A crowned woman points accusingly at a distraught nymph being restrained by companions at the center. Around them, more nymphs bathe and gather near a stone fountain topped by a small statue, while an archer with a hunting dog stands at the far right beneath a swath of golden drapery. Titian painted this scene in the 1550s; it belongs to the National Gallery.
items.tags: mythology, diana, callisto, nymphs, fountain, oil painting, renaissance

items.title: Nymph and Shepherd
items.description_narrative: A nude woman reclines on an animal pelt in a shadowy clearing, her body turned away as a young shepherd holding a pipe leans close beside her. A blasted, leafless tree trunk rises behind them, and small grazing animals dot the pale hillside in the distance. Titian painted this pastoral scene around the 1570s; it belongs to the Kunsthistorisches Museum.
items.tags: pastoral, nymph, shepherd, reclining nude, landscape, oil painting

items.title: Portrait of Philip II
items.description_narrative: A young man in an elaborately padded black doublet trimmed with fur and gold studs rests one hand on a red-draped table, the other resting on the hilt of a sword. A fine gold chain hangs at his throat above a white fur collar, and his expression is composed and reserved. This portrait of Philip II of Spain, from the workshop of Titian, dates to the 16th century; it belongs to the Museo del Prado.
items.tags: portrait, philip ii, spanish court, oil painting, state portrait

items.title: The Bacchanal of the Andrians
items.description_narrative: A crowd of revelers drinks and dances beneath tall trees, one man raising a silver ewer overhead while a boy pours wine at their feet. In the foreground, a nude woman sleeps sprawled across the grass, oblivious to the music and movement around her, and a ship sails calmly on the sea behind. Titian painted this bacchanal between about 1523 and 1526.
items.tags: bacchanal, mythology, revelers, nude figure, landscape, oil painting

items.title: An Idyll: A Mother and a Halberdier in a Wooded Landscape
items.description_narrative: A woman in a pale dress sits beneath a leafy tree, a nude infant nestled in her lap, while at right a young soldier in armor stands holding a tall halberd topped with a small pennant. Behind them, a cluster of farm buildings and a tower rise on a gentle hillside under a soft evening sky. This pastoral scene is attributed to Titian, painted in the 16th century; it belongs to the Harvard Art Museums.
items.tags: pastoral scene, mother and child, soldier, landscape, oil painting, renaissance

items.title: Penitent Magdalene
items.description_narrative: A woman with long, loose red-gold hair looks upward with parted lips, one hand pressed to her bare chest in a gesture of penitence. Her hair falls in thick waves nearly covering her body, and a small silver vase sits on a ledge beside her, with a patch of stormy blue sky visible behind. Titian and his workshop painted this around 1540; it belongs to the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux.
items.tags: penitent magdalene, religious figure, portrait, oil painting, renaissance
items.credit_line: Own work by Tylwyth Eldar. Taken on 30 October 2024, 11:43:29.

items.title: Tarquin and Lucretia
items.description_narrative: A man lunges forward with a dagger while a nude woman recoils against piled white bedclothes, one arm thrown up to ward him off. The scene renders the Roman legend of Tarquin and Lucretia, painted by Titian in the 1570s and now held by the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux.
items.tags: italian renaissance, mythology, roman history, titian, oil painting, violence
items.credit_line: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux, Bx E 42; Wikidata Q18822501

items.title: Mars, Venus and Cupid
items.description_narrative: A bearded man in armor leans in to kiss a reclining nude woman, her hand resting on his head as they embrace beneath a leafy tree. Below them, a helmet and sword rest against fabric, while at right a winged child flies off holding a bow, quiver, and arrow. Titian painted this mythological scene around 1550; it belongs to the Kunsthistorisches Museum.
items.tags: mythology, mars and venus, embrace, cupid, oil painting, renaissance

items.title: Portrait of a Man
items.description_narrative: A bearded man in a dark, fur-trimmed coat glances slightly to one side, his loose white collar catching soft light against the deep shadow behind him. His hair falls in soft waves to his shoulders, and his expression is calm and reserved. Titian painted this portrait in the 16th century.
items.tags: portrait, bearded man, dark background, oil painting, venetian

items.title: Venus with an Organ Player and a Dog
items.description_narrative: An organist glances over his shoulder at a nude woman reclining beside him, a winged child resting against her shoulder. A small white dog sits at the foot of the bed, and heavy red drapery hangs above while a distant landscape opens through the space behind the organ pipes. This painting is attributed to Titian, made around 1550.
items.tags: venus, organ player, dog, cupid, oil painting
items.credit_line: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202.

items.title: The Triumph of Love
items.description_narrative: A winged child stands triumphant atop a crouching lion, one foot planted on its back, bow raised in one hand and an arrow in the other. A quiver of arrows hangs at his hip, and a wide, hazy landscape with a distant town and hills fills the circular background. Titian painted this tondo around 1545; it belongs to the Ashmolean Museum.
items.tags: triumph of love, cupid, allegory, tondo, landscape
